significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—languages with lower refusal activation on matched harmful prompts have higher jailbreak success—together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which a "mostly shared refusal direction" and language-varying triggering account for that behavior. This fixes expectations across languages and links the behavioral low-resource disparity reported by Yong et al. to the causal refusal-direction account of Arditi et al.; it establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism, although the wording that a "lower" threshold makes prompts less likely to cross it is internally ambiguous. A negative result would rule out this shared-direction/threshold explanation of the safety gap, but would not distinguish among multi-component alternatives; true and false outcomes are otherwise distinguishable through the asserted overlap, resource ordering, failure coupling, and intervention effect. Topic-substitution check: the generic multilingual-representation topic would not earn this score, because the specific activation-to-jailbreak relation and threshold-equalization consequence are what raise it above the obvious shared-versus-language-specific representation hypothesis.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the "per-language refusal-trigger thresholds," "jailbreak success vs activation" diagnostic, and the intervention to "add the shared refusal direction / equalize threshold"; these could support auditing and mitigation rather than merely description. The diagnostic is primarily contemporaneous or post hoc as written—the claim does not explicitly promise prediction before a jailbreak attempt—but threshold adjustment is a deployment-facing control that could be applied before generation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive resource-level ordering and activation–jailbreak coupling predict what should recur, so more than a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction survives recalibration, though cross-architecture and training-regime scope is unstated. Topic-substitution check: multilingual safety alone would not justify this reach; the transferable measurable relation and named direction-level mitigation support uptake by model auditors and deployers.
